title: Flywheel Effect
equation: Momentum = Disciplined Pushes per Month × Months Sustained
hook: There's no single push that makes a business take off. It's a hundred boring ones in a row.
statement: Momentum comes from small, consistent pushes that build on each other over time.
explainer: In a good loop, each step makes the next one easier. Lower prices bring more customers, more customers bring more sellers. It feels slow for a while, then it spins on its own.
sop: Map the loop where each step makes the next one easier.
Find the one activity that adds the most energy to it.
Repeat it every week, even when results look flat.
Track the total effect over months, not single wins.
Ignore shiny new ideas that pull you off the loop.
equation_example: 12 Disciplined Pushes per Month × 24 Months Sustained = 288. A higher, rising number means the loop is starting to feed itself. Low or falling means you're still pushing dead weight instead of a spinning wheel.
question: Draw your business loop in four steps, then circle the step that needs a steady push right now.
closing_statement: Momentum comes from repetition, not intensity.
